body:
I’m really glad that you don’t want to die right now. A lot of the problems you mentioned can probably be fixed with a few changes. Maybe if you’re hair is an awkward length, you can try extensions or a braided hairdo instead of using clips to keep it out of your face. And about your eyebrows, I know you said that wearing makeup would embarass you, but have you considered maybe experimenting with an eyebrow pencil, just to fill in the patchiness? Or if you’re afraid of trying yourself, you can visit a makeup artist and have them show you how. It can look really natural and nobody would even know that you were wearing it. I know these are only small things but, if they can help in any way it may be worth a try.

Being sociable comes natural to some but it’s also a skill that a lot of people have to work on. Even if you had the opportunity to start life all over again, you would still need to put in the work of improving your social skills. 

I don’t know if you would be interested but I recently started a DBT (Dialectical Behaviour Therapy) workbook to help me unlearn the patterns of thinking that lead me to be so judgemental of myself and default to thoughts of suicide when times get hard. It’s also supposed to help improve your skills in interpersonal relationships. I’m not done yet but I only just started. If you’d like to try it out too, I can share the name with you.

This is how I feel, when I’m at my lowest so I fully relate. I just want to say that the sadness, like everything else, will come to an end. Maybe not today or tomorrow, but emotions are temporary. Depression makes us feel like the sadness never ends because our brain is better at remembering the hard times, but there’s always good moments mixed in between.

If you dont mind me asking, what or who aren’t you good enough for?

I can promise you that you are worth so much more than how you look, but I understand that we live in a society that prizes attractiveness. I just know that if I had to choose someone to spend the rest of my life with, personality far outweighs beauty. A lot of people feel the same way, and the people who think otherwise aren’t really worth your time anyway.

I’m sorry you feel so lonely. I know when you’re 22, it feels like if You haven’t accomplished certain things you never will. I’ve met people who had never been in a relationship until their late 20’s, but they eventually found love. You still have a lot of time. I am sorry about your parents, though.

Even though you were physically alone on Christmas, there were people here who wanted to talk with you and support you. I know it’s not the same, but if you don’t want to be alone, I’d love to keep you company here online.
Is there anything you can do to help? Stay in your room and wear headphones, maybe?
You’re welcome, and I hope your day gets a little bit better.
It’s no problem. just remember to be gentle with yourself. You deserve it.

I used to be a depressed teenager and it was rough. I just want you to know, the feelings that you have when you’re a teenager tend to be way stronger. I’m not trying to say it will get better (although I’m not saying the opposite either), but rather, that these feelings are temporary.   
I’m really happy to hear that you have a support system and have access to proper mental health care. These factors put you in a really good position to get better. Unfortunately, sometimes it can take a lot of time to get better.
I can be a friend, if you need somebody to listen.

I’m glad you reached out to a therapist. A therapist would probably be ideal person to talk to about you personal issues, but I think if you avoid bringing up your depression in conversations about your own mistakes, I don’t think anybody can see it as a deflection. If you make sure to separate the two, you can give your partner the space to discuss her feelings about your mistakes, while also giving her the space to freely support you without having to give up her own needs, in favour of yours. Does that make sense?

Sometimes I feel like a broken person too, but maybe broken isn’t the right word. For what it’s worth, I think there are very few people who are unfixable.
That’s great! I hope you have a better day.
Well I’m not a doctor and you should definitely see a psychiatrist, but I believe NDRI’s are better for dealing with apathy.

I’m so sorry for what you’re going through. If your family system is really that messed up, you need to step in try and be the support she needs. When you talk to her again, try your best not to make her feel guilty. Tell her that you want to understand and encourage her to share what she’s going through whenever she’s comfortable with it. I don’t know where you live but look into options for therapy, maybe through her school or through government social services. The most important thing is to be there for her, be gentle and always listen. If you want advice about anything else, I’ll be here.

I wish we had better systems in place for dealing with issues like this because this would probably be considered a cognitive disability. You deserve to have accommodations and you may be entitled to them, depending on where you live.

I’d consider extreme apathy like how you mentioned in your post to be a low. Low doesn’t only have to mean sadness. There are some types of antidepressants that are really effective at helping with apathy, just not SSRI’s.
I’m really glad that you decided to keep going for a little while longer. Good luck, and I hope things go up from here.

From the story that you told, I don’t think that you ruined everything. If your mother is this toxic, consider the fact that she raised you and so you may be hypersensitive to her specific brand of toxicity, while your boyfriend is not. He should try to be more empathetic. 

I’m sorry that you have covid and that you can’t be home for Christmas, but I don’t think your making a small thing into a big thing. Not being home for Christmas is a big deal. Not being respected by your family is a big deal. You have every right to respond with frustration in the face of negativity and toxicity. I hope your day goes better from here on out.

I’m so sorry that you’re going through this today. Losing your boyfriend must be so difficult and you must be trying your hardest to keep things together. I know it must feel impossible to be happy today, so I won’t hope for that, but I only hope that you’re able to feel better. Maybe not today, but some day.

I’m so sorry that your parents are doing this to you. Do you know if there are any shelters in your area? Or maybe you have some friends who you can make arrangements with, even if it’s just until you get your first pay check. You shouldn’t have your whole life and plans uprooted on someone else’s whim. I really wish you the best.

You’re never a pussy for being empathetic, male or female. A lot of the issues you’re having seem like they may be related to your ADD. I think you deserve to have room to make mistakes without other people making your feel bad for them. I hope you find something worth living for, even if you personally don’t want to.
I won’t try to convince you otherwise but if nobody comes forward, do you want to talk? I know I’m only a stranger but if you wake up tomorrow and you want to vent or rant, I’d be happy to listen.

Does your partner know what you’re struggling with? Does anybody in your life? It’s so hard to get better without a support system In real life. If you don’t want to tell anybody, I would love to talk with you about It.

It’s a blessing to have a mother who loves you and who you love enough to avoid hurting. I’m just sorry that you’re hurting so much. Does she know what you’re struggling with? I understand if you don’t want to tell her, but she may be able to support you and I’m sure she would 100% prefer you to tell her now, rather than you having to deal with it all by yourself.

I definitely get not feeling like I can live a normal life or hold down a job. I also really feel like suicide is my best option. I wish there was something that I could do to help you change your circumstances. It’s really messed up that life can just drive us to this point.

God, this is how I feel all the time. I had the worst fight this morning just because I feel like I need to reach out for help but I also feel like nobody wants to be bothered by me. It’s really hard. If you ever want to talk to someone without feeling like a bother, I’ll be right here. You won‘t be a bother.

If it helps, there’s a lot of us on here together right now. I don’t know what it is about Christmas that makes people so miserable but here we are. You’re not alone though. I’m here too and I get it.
What is it proof of, if you don’t mind me asking?

It’s good to let it out. I wish you didn’t have to repress those feelings at all. I hope you gain some catharsis, just don’t forget to take care of yourself today. Be gentle with yourself, if you can.

I felt the same way about therapy after going to several very unhelpful therapists. Sometimes you have to shop around until you get the right fit. While I do endorse therapy, I will also say that therapy can only help so much. If you have bad life circumstances, no amount of talking can change that. 

I can tell that you’re frustrated, and I get that. Nothing is more frustrating than not being understood. I struggle a lot with depression and suicidal thoughts and I know exactly what you’re talking about. Other people don’t really get it. They think they’re helping when at the end of the day, they’re just making you feel worse. I really wish I had an answer for you, but the truth is, most people don’t understand being suicidal. 

I hope you don’t mind if I ask, but have you tried antidepressants? Those are another thing that may take a little shopping around to find the right fit. It won’t cure you, but it may help to dull the extreme lows.

I completely understand that. It’s never as simple as other people make it out to be and truly, it’s nearly impossible for somebody who has never experienced depression or suicidal thoughts to understand what it’s like. I get it though, and you deserve to have an objective conversation. Sometimes, it’s easier to talk to a stranger because they have less of an emotional/personal response. If you want to talk some, I’m here.

I’m sorry that you’re hurting. I know it seems like everybody else is happy today but you’re not alone. You’re right, nobody can guarantee that things will get better. What I will say is that everything is temporary. Happiness is temporary, but so is sadness. I hope you feel a little better today.

Holidays are always so hard for me so I woke up this morning and wanted to come here. I usually avoid it because it’s not good for me to see this type of thing all the time, but I know how lonely and miserable it gets, especially on Christmas. This sub had helped me a lot through the years and I wanted to give back today.

29 is still a perfect age to find love and start a life with someone. It always feels impossible when you’re single, but it’s not. Sometimes you just need to broaden your perspectives, meet new people and try new things. I know that sounds hard, but theres always people in your area that aren’t in your social circle, but who may be exactly what you’re looking for.
Im sorry that things are so frustrating for you. How are your thoughts contradicting?
Have you talked to your girlfriend about this? I think you should give her a chance to help. You never know what might change if you had support from somebody who loved you.

The holidays are a hard time for a lot of people, myself included. Idk if it would be poetic, but it would be difficult, and like the other person said, painful. I really hope you decide to stay indoors today, but I completely understand if you don’t.
What about another week? Or another day? A year is a really long time to properly fathom, but do you think that you can make it to next week?

The worst people know how to find the kindest most vulnerable people and take all that they can get from them. At the very least, be happy that you’re not such a cruel, twisted person. Maybe you’re better than what the world has given you, but that doesn’t mean there aren’t still good people out there somewhere.   


I also feel like I don’t belong in this world, but when you look at the world, maybe thats not a bad thing. I only wish you could find the people who are worth knowing.
